# `bootstrap/` — the emission a repository has before it has any mathematics

`empty-repo.json` is a valid `emission/1.0` in every respect except the two
vacuity constraints: `constants: []`, and every count zero. It is what the
emitter produces in a repository generated by `mfc init` and not yet written
in, and it is the only shape `bootstrap: true` excuses.

It carries no `$comment` key of its own, and that is not an oversight —
`emission-1.0.schema.json` sets `additionalProperties: false`, so a fixture
that documented itself inline would be rejected for the wrong reason and would
stop testing what it is here to test. Hence this file.

Do not confuse it with `../invalid/empty-emission.json`. That one has a
constant and `counts.in_scope: 0` — a **mis-scoped emitter**, which swept
something real and matched none of it against the root library. Bootstrap does
not excuse that at any age of a repository, and `test_bootstrap.py` asserts so.
